name: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms associated with eosinophilia and abnormalities of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 or JAK2
aliases: MLN with eosinophilia and PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 or JAK2 rearrangement
Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with eosinophilia and tyrosine kinase fusion genes

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2022)

criteria.description: Detection of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, or JAK2 gene rearrangements or fusion transcripts by molecular genetic testing
Bone marrow biopsy showing myeloid/lymphoid proliferation with eosinophilia and absence of other defining genetic abnormalities
Exclusion of other myeloid neoplasms such as chronic eosinophilic leukemia not otherwise specified
Presence of clinical features consistent with myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm such as splenomegaly or constitutional symptoms

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of persistent eosinophilia and detection of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, or JAK2 gene rearrangement with supportive bone marrow morphology
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular genetic confirmation is essential for diagnosis and guides targeted therapy.

pathognomonic.notes: Marked and persistent eosinophilia is characteristic
searchTerms: high levels of eosinophils in blood
elevated white blood cells called eosinophils

pathognomonic.symptomName: Presence of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 or JAK2 fusion gene
searchTerms: presence of fusion genes in blood cells
genetic abnormalities involving PDGFRA or JAK2

common.symptomName: Constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Bone marrow hypercellularity with eosinophilic proliferation
searchTerms: bone marrow with too many cells

common.symptomName: Cutaneous manifestations including pruritus and rash
common.notes: Occasionally observed due to eosinophil infiltration

searchTerms: lung tissue changes causing breathing issues

occasional.symptomName: Neurological symptoms such as peripheral neuropathy
occasional.notes: Due to eosinophilic infiltration or paraneoplastic effects
May cause abdominal pain or diarrhea

rare.symptomName: Renal impairment secondary to eosinophilic infiltration
Psychiatric symptoms such as cognitive impairment

laboratory: Bone marrow hypercellularity with eosinophilic proliferation
Elevated serum tryptase in PDGFRA rearranged cases
imaging: Splenomegaly on abdominal ultrasound or CT
Pulmonary infiltrates on chest X-ray or CT
genetic: Detection of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, or JAK2 gene rearrangements by FISH, RT-PCR or NGS
Identification of fusion transcripts involving tyrosine kinase genes
other: Response to tyrosine kinase inhibitors (e.g., imatinib) in PDGFRA/PDGFRB cases
Histopathological confirmation by bone marrow biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Absence of PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1 or JAK2 rearrangements
Less responsive to tyrosine kinase inhibitors

redFlags: Rapidly progressive eosinophilia with organ dysfunction
Cardiac involvement with signs of heart failure
Neurological deficits suggestive of eosinophilic infiltration
references: Arber DA, et al. WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 5th Edition, 2022.
Gotlib J. World Health Organization-defined eosinophilic disorders: 2017 update on diagnosis, risk stratification, and management. Am J Hematol. 2017.
